conventions.convention: Throughout the partition page, n counts balls or domain elements, k counts boxes or codomain values, partitions are written in nonincreasing order, and Ferrers diagrams use English convention with the longest row on top.
The empty partition is the unique partition of 0, has zero parts and largest part 0; p(0)=1, p(n)=0 for n<0, and p_k(n)=0 when n<0 or k<0, with p_0(0)=1.
A colouring action is the left action (g·f)(x)=f(g^{-1}x); colouring weights take values in a commutative ring and multiply over positions.
The cycle index averages, over all acting group elements, the monomial whose exponent of s_d is the number of d-cycles in the induced permutation.
The cycle-index series starts at n=0 and uses the normalization 1/n! for the S_n-action in degree n.

The strong Erdős–Hajnal property is required only for graphs in the hereditary class having at least two vertices, and requires disjoint linear-sized sides forming either a complete or an anticomplete pair.
A co-leaf is a leaf in the complement, equivalently a vertex of degree |V(G)|−2 in G.
Mixed-block reachability relates equal blocks and blocks joined by a finite chain of consecutive mixed pairs.
A quotient blockade replaces each mixed-reachability class by the union of its member blocks and orders quotient blocks by their least original block index.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite action G on an n-element set, Z_G(s_1,…,s_n)=(1/|G|)∑_{g∈G}∏_{d=1}^n s_d^{j_d(g)}.
n counts balls or domain elements, k counts boxes or codomain values; unlabelled occupancies are reordered nonincreasingly with zeros omitted.
p(n) counts partitions of n with p(0)=1 and p(n)=0 for n<0; p_k(n) counts partitions into exactly k positive parts with the stated zero boundary conventions.
A group element with cycle counts j_d fixes m^{∑j_d} unweighted colourings, and its weighted fixed-colouring sum is ∏_d p_d^{j_d}.
For a finite action G on X and an m-colour set, the number of colouring orbits is Z_G(m,m,…,m).
For weights in a commutative ring, |G| times the pattern inventory equals ∑_{g∈G}∏_d p_d^{j_d(g)}; when 1/|G| exists, the inventory is Z_G(p_1,…,p_|X|).
For positive n and k, the twelve labelled/unlabelled and arbitrary/injective/surjective placement counts are the twelve formulas listed in the Statement.
For every integer n≥0, there is a bijection between partitions of n into odd parts and partitions of n into distinct parts.
A hereditary class has the strong Erdős–Hajnal property if one ε>0 gives every member with at least two vertices a disjoint pure pair whose two sides each have size at least ε|V(G)|.
Every hereditary class of finite graphs with the strong Erdős–Hajnal property also has the Erdős–Hajnal property.
For every integer k≥2, there exists γ_k>0 such that every finite graph with no induced P_k and no induced complement of P_k contains a pure pair with both sides of size at least γ_k|V(G)|.
Two blocks are related when they are equal or can be joined by a finite chain of consecutive mixed block pairs.
The quotient blockade consists of the unions of the mixed-reachability equivalence classes, ordered by least original index.
If u is mixed on a quotient block D but pure to each original block in D, then two mixed original blocks in D make u complete to one and anticomplete to the other.

concerns.concern: The Statement quantifies over every finite graph but omits the |V(G)|≥2 condition present in the strong-property definition and used in the proof. For G=K1, which is P_k- and complement-P_k-free for k≥2, γ_k|V(G)|>0 forces two nonempty disjoint sides, which is impossible.

Step 1.1 displays ∑_j ε_{m,j}2^j m=c_m, but the left side equals m c_m. The intended size-preservation calculation needs m c_m on the right; as written, the proof contains a false computation whenever m≠1 and c_m≠0.

Distinct parts and odd parts are defined only in the paragraph beginning “For a nonempty partition,” but p_dist(0) and p_odd(0) are then used throughout n≥0 statements and product series. The file never declares that the empty partition belongs to both restricted families.

This owned item and six other forest/leaf-deletion A-items are absent from the A-page list, while two corresponding examples are absent from the B-page list. Several omitted theorems also default to proved_here:true although their local “proof” merely repeats the external source theorem as [F1]. The page prose acknowledges blockers, but the generated group scope still owns these items.

The formula λ′_j=|{i:λ_i≥j}| does not state the required range 1≤j≤λ_1. Read literally for all positive j, it produces trailing zeros rather than a finite partition; a reader supplies the standard range.

The symmetry and transitivity steps assume each related pair is witnessed by a mixed chain, but the definition also permits relation by equality. The cases A=B, B=C, or A=B in the two transitivity premises are not separated, although they are immediate.

The inverse construction says only that a_i≥d−i and strict decrease make the symmetric diagonal hooks “nest to form a Ferrers diagram.” This is the substantive well-definedness step of the inverse and needs a short row-length or Frobenius-coordinate verification.
The item id and generated inventory call this a four-block configuration, but the file title and construction use exactly three original blocks A_1, A_2, and B.
